title: Total Quality Management for IT: Main Exam, 21 December 2018
instructions: ANSWER ALL QUESTIONS IN SECTION A AND ANY OTHER TWO FROM SECTION B.

parts.text: What do you understand by software quality? Explain how quality can be a source of competitive advantage to an organization.
Briefly describe the four critical pillars of TQM that are essential in implementing TQM in a service company.
Highlight five benefits that an organization can derive from ISO registration.
Explain why Six Sigma quality control is considered unique by organizations that embrace total quality management.
Explain the principles that guide the success of a total quality management programme.
Most organizations are abandoning traditional management and adopting total quality management. Explain the differences between total quality management and traditional management.
Organizations that have embraced total quality management have found themselves better than those that have not. Explain the advantages of embracing total quality management.
Clearly explain any ten dimensions of quality.
Total quality management is all about continuous process improvement. Define continuous process improvement and discuss the various phases of continuous process improvement.
Garvin (1984) developed a conceptual framework for categorizing the approaches used to define quality. Explain any two of his perspectives.
Explain the various factors that consumers take into consideration before they make a purchase.

For organizations to succeed in improving the quality of their products and services, it is important that they get feedback from customers. Define customer feedback and explain the various tools that can be used to collect information.
The American Society for Quality Control (1971) categorized quality costs into four categories. Outline those categories.
Briefly explain four different ways in which software engineering can ensure software quality.
Define the term business process re-design or re-engineering (BPR).
Discuss the seven phases in business process re-design or re-engineering (BPR).
Highlight different ways in which the quality of computer software can be evaluated.
